items.title: Trump hid in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
items.description: The US president was reportedly part of a ruse where reporters were falsely told he was with them on Air Force One leaving a Nato summit in Turkey.

items.title: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
items.description: Ukraine's president says strikes in Zaporizhzhia - which killed at least six and injured 19 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally.

items.title: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
items.description: The ex-president is convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.

items.title: At least 169 killed in Colombia's largest earthquake in years
items.description: More than 480 people were injured in the quakes, with more feared trapped under collapsed buildings.

items.title: Luigi Mangione back in court as key questions remain over case ahead of murder trial
items.description: Mangione's lawyers have yet to signal their defence, while prosecutors are in a battle over evidence.

items.title: Lebanon parliament votes to abolish death penalty
items.description: The new law - which next goes to the cabinet for approval - would make Lebanon the first country in the Middle East to end capital punishment.

items.title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
items.description: Cold calling is coming to an end in France, with one consumer group calling the ban a "small revolution".

items.title: Houthis kill three in first deadly attack since start of Iran war - reports
items.description: The attack was reportedly carried out by Iranian proxy on a small cargo ship, as tensions in region over the US-Iran conflict remain high.

items.title: Drone captures devastating aftermath of Spokane wildfires
items.description: The aerial footage shows homes destroyed down to their foundations, with burned cars still parked in some driveways.

items.title: Thailand suspends new gun permits after mass shooting
items.description: Authorities promise tough new laws in the country, which has high levels of firearms ownership.

items.title: Libyan authorities battle big blaze at major oil refinery
items.description: Monday's drone strike on the Zawiya refinery was the third such incident in two days.

items.title: Australia PM under fire for remarks on Japanese counterpart's melon gifts
items.description: An ex-Japanese envoy said the "sexist" comments "betrayed the close bond" between the countries.

items.title: Canada flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seat belt
items.description: The incident has sparked a debate over child safety and discipline on commercial planes.

items.title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
items.description: The American Academy of Pediatrics calls the recommendation on measles, mumps and rubella shots "dangerous".

items.title: Watch: What we know about Tupac murder suspect Duane 'Keffe D' Davis
items.description: The trial of the 63-year-old former gang boss kicked off on Monday, and he has entered a not guilty plea.

items.title: Jackie, the famous California bald eagle, dies after weeks of intensive care
items.description: Jackie and her partner, Shadow, had been watched by millions of people over the years through the Big Bear Eagle Nest Cam.

items.title: New train service connects Finland and Sweden for first time in decades
items.description: The service will enable rail travel from Portugal to Lapland - what is believed to be the longest train journey in Europe.

items.title: The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA
items.description: After the Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham said it was "common sense" to ban transgender women from women's sports, a row has emerged in the WNBA - with former NBA players saying eligibility rules mean they can enter the 2027 Draft.

items.title: The lonely Chinese men being conned by fake brides
items.description: "Flash marriage" scams are an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis long in the making in China.

items.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
items.description: The government is trying to attribute blame for the unprecedented fires which tore through the country last month.
